question: Why does the rule "A function should do one thing" matter in a code review?

expected_rule_sections.heading: A function should do one thing
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 1: PR review rules
A function should do one thing

relevant_concepts: A function should do one thing
"One thing" is subjective, so test it: if the function has more than one reason to change, it does more than one thing. Mixed responsibilities are harder to name, test, and change safely.

question: What review guidance applies to "Avoid hidden side effects and unrelated work"?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Avoid hidden side effects and unrelated work
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 1: PR review rules
Avoid hidden side effects and unrelated work

relevant_concepts: Avoid hidden side effects and unrelated work
Reading should be predictable: the control flow follows the apparent purpose, and the routine does not hide unrelated work. Hidden effects cause surprises that are hard to debug.

question: Why does the rule "Routines should do what a reader expects" matter in a code review?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Routines should do what a reader expects
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 1: PR review rules
Routines should do what a reader expects

relevant_concepts: Routines should do what a reader expects
Clean code is code you read and simply agree with from top to bottom. Predictability means the code communicates its decisions clearly, even when the logic isn't trivial.
